transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. You know? Like, dying would just be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family and my crew. I mean, my crew... we were laying down this beautiful ceramic tile last week in this big custom kitchen out in the suburbs. The lady of the house was so particular, she wanted everything just so, you know how they get with the grout lines. I swear, picking the right grout color is harder than picking out a car for some people. I used to drive this old Chevy truck, actually, back when I first started taking classes at the community college. It had this weird rattle in the steering column, but it got me to class and back. Anyway, yeah, I just... I think they'd all be better off if I was just gone.
Have you ever had a distinct period when your mood was unusually elevated or irritable?

Elevated? Like... happy? No, I don't think so. I haven't felt happy in... well, it feels like forever. My husband, he used to say I was the life of the party when we first met. We met at this little dive bar downtown, they had this incredible jukebox. You don't see jukeboxes anymore, do you? Now everyone just plays music from their phones. I miss the physical buttons, you know? The satisfying click when you pick a song. It's kind of like the click of a good tile cutter when you score a piece perfectly. But no, I haven't felt like that in a long time. Mostly I just feel... heavy. And I know the voices agree with me, they tell me I'm dragging everyone down.
Before this current period of depression, have you ever had a separate period when you were depressed like this?

Before this? I... I'm not really sure. It just feels like it's been this way forever, honestly. Everything just sort of blurs together into this big, heavy, gray block of time. Kind of like... well, kind of like when you have to lay down a hundred square feet of that cheap gray commercial carpet. We did this whole office building last year, just miles and miles of this boring gray loop pile. 

It's so heavy, too. People don't realize how heavy carpet is until they try to move a roll of it. My old boss, Dave, he used to make us carry it up the stairs instead of using the freight elevator because he said it built character. Can you believe that? Built character. My knees are completely shot now because of him. I actually took a semester of physical therapy classes back at the community college because I thought maybe I could switch careers, you know, help people with their joints instead of ruining my own. But the anatomy textbook was so expensive, and the memorization was just... a lot. I think I still have that book in a box in my garage somewhere, under all my extra trowels. 

I'm sorry, what did you ask me? About being like this before? I really don't know. It's hard to remember a time when I didn't just feel... weighed down.
Before this current period, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt substantially better and were no longer depressed?

Substantially better? Two months? No, no... it's been pretty constant. I know exactly how long it's been, actually. It's been about a year and two months. It started a few months after my husband's injury. 

He hurt his back, you see. Not on the job, though. He was trying to move this antique armoire we found at a flea market. It was gorgeous, solid mahogany, beautiful brass handles. You just don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is particle board and veneer from IKEA. I remember we went to IKEA once, just to look around, and we got so lost in that maze they set up. We ended up buying like, thirty of those little tealight candles and a fake potted plant. The meatballs were good, though. Have you had their meatballs? They serve them with this lingonberry jam. It sounds weird, meat and jam, but it really works. Kind of sweet and savory. 

Anyway, yeah, he slipped on the porch stairs carrying that armoire and just... crack. So he's been out of work, and I've been trying to take on extra jobs, but the depression... it's just been sitting on my chest since then. A year and two months of this.
When you say the voices tell you that you’re dragging everyone down, do you hear them as voices that seem to come from outside your own thoughts?

Yeah, they... they sound completely real. Like someone is actually in the room with me. Usually, it's this man's voice, and it always seems to come from right behind me. Like, I'll be at a job site, laying down some ceramic tile—which, by the way, is so much harder than porcelain to get a clean cut on. Porcelain is denser, you know? It's fired at a higher temperature. My first big solo job was this beautiful porcelain subway tile backsplash in this huge kitchen remodel. The homeowner was this lady who collected vintage teapots. She had shelves and shelves of them, all different shapes. One looked like a little cottage, another was shaped like a cat. I always wondered how you clean the inside of the cat one, the spout was so narrow. You'd probably need one of those tiny pipe cleaners, like the ones kids use for crafts. I used to love making things with pipe cleaners when I was little. We'd make little stick figures and bend their arms and legs. 

But yeah, I'll be working, or even just in my own kitchen, and I'll hear him right over my shoulder. He says things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." It's so clear, I always whip around to see who snuck up on me, but... there's never anyone there. It's just me. And the teapots, I guess, if I'm at that one house. But mostly just me.
